During this Holy Week, let us remember what the Bible says about fair and living wages. Isaiah 58.6 says that God wants us to "break the chains of injustice," "end exploitation in the workplace," and "set the oppressed free." "cancel debts." The McDonald's announcement that it will raise wages for 90,000 employees is a big win for fast-food cooks and cashiers, and for all of us who support them. By standing together, fast-food workers are making it less acceptable for profitable companies like McDonald's to pay wages so low that its workers are trapped in poverty.

The Golden State might soon be about the color of California's lawns. Governor Jerry Brown announced on Wednesday that he is making water restrictions mandatory for residents, businesses, and farms. He ordered cities and towns in the drought-ravaged state to reduce their water usage by 25%. "We're in a new era," Brown said. "The idea of your nice little green grass getting lots of water every day, that's going to be a thing of the past." The 25% cut in usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-feet of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

It is almost time for people in the UK to vote. polling stations are ready to open. This election might change how the country is governed. The campaign was very short, especially compared to US standards, where candidates take years to prepare. The result could give power to Ed Miliband’s Labour Party, taking it from David Cameron’s Conservative government. Or, leaders might struggle to make deals with smaller parties. We will know the outcome when voting ends late Thursday evening, local time.

This is the time of year when more than 2 billion Christians around the world are thinking about the death and resurrection of Jesus. This Holy Week, we are asking Christians to also remember the terrible things happening to believers today. On Thursday, Christian college students in Kenya were killed in a attack. Christians in other countries are still in danger.

 Religious extremists are targeting hundreds of thousands of Christians and other people just because of their faith. These extremists are crucing, be, st, forcing into slavery, sexually abusing, trafficking, bombing, and forcing people to leave their homes.

The Washington Post has released emails that are racist and offensive. These emails caused three employees in Ferguson, Missouri, to either quit or lose their jobs. The emails were found during an investigation by the U.S. Department of Justice into racial bias in the city's police and courts. The messages contain offensive comments about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails on Thursday through a public records request, and CNN reviewed them on Friday. The emails involve Police Captain Rick Henke and a Sergeant.

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia. The police found at least 55 dead dogs dumped in the bush in Queensland. According to Australian media reports, the two people from Bundaberg, a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman, are each charged with illegally possessing a firearm. The woman was also charged with blocking the police. Michael Beatty, who speaks for RSPCA Queensland, told ABC that the investigation is still ongoing. The animal rights group is helping the Queensland police with their investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in Wisconsin. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free options, in stores near Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. This week, their business was in trouble because people confused them with Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. That other pizza shop made news because its owners said they would not cater a same-sex wedding. Angry people left comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called their phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton, believed to have been used by Ottoman soldiers during the 17th century siege of Vienna, has been discovered under a cellar in Austria. The remains were found by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni) during a construction site for a shopping center in Tulln between 2006 and 2007. Alfred Galik, an archaeozoologist, said that the partially uncovered skeleton was initially thought to be a large horse or cattle. "But one look at the cervical vertebrae, the lower jaw and the metacarpal bones immediately revealed that this was a camel."

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died on Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. his parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, released a statement confirming the death. They asked the media and the public to respect the family's privacy during this difficult time. Ed Winter, an assistant chief in the Los Angeles County coroner's office, told CNN affiliate KTLA that Getty's death appears to be due to natural causes or an accident. Some medication was found in Getty's home, but investigators do not know if he was taking it or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, which killed everyone on board. The latest report says he made the plane’s descent faster. It is a terrible event. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much Lubitz hid his mental illness and how much help he asked for. We need to ask: how did his depression affect his ability to fly? Should he have quit his job? Should his doctors have raised warnings? His case brings up important questions about people with mental illnesses and the shame they often feel.

On April 8, 2015, CNN Student News covered several stories. The show discussed a report about U.S.-Cuba relations, and then gave more details about California’s historic drought. The drought’s effects are increasingly affecting the entire country. The news also reported about a flu outbreak in Chicago, but this flu does not affect humans. Additionally, there is a plan to build a tunnel connecting Denmark and Germany with an underwater road and railway. On this page, you can find the transcript of today’s show and a place to request to be part of the CNN Student News Roll Call. Click here to read the transcript of today’s CNN Student News program.

A man who did not want to give his name was caught because of a tattoo on his neck. The tattoo was the name "Gertrude." This was what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor. Taylor is a 23-year-old man who was convicted of murder and escaped from jail before being arrested in Chicago overnight.

Police in Illinois had been searching for Taylor since early Wednesday. He had jumped a correctional officer at the Jerome Combs Detention Center in Kankakee. Then, he ran away wearing the guard's uniform and driving the guard's SUV.

 Surveillance video was the last thing officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight on Friday in Chicago. "They saw a guy that matched the description," Buk

Prince Harry, who is 30 years old and is finishing his military career, is going to Australia. He arrives on Monday for a four-week stay. The Australian military says he will work and live with soldiers in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. He has already spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10 years in the military.

The Florida Attorney General’s office announced on Thursday that two corrections officers and one former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate who was about to be released from prison. These men used to work as guards in Florida prisons.

According to CNN affiliate WJXT, an FBI informant met with them after going undercover in a branch of the Ku Klux Klan called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan. Court documents state that Thomas Jordan Driver, 25, told the informant that he had fought with the inmate and that he and David Elliot Moran, 47, wanted the inmate dead ("six feet under").

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A series of intense negotiations concluded on Thursday in Lausanne. The P5+1, a group of world powers, reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. The success of this agreement is uncertain. The parties have until the end of June to finalize the details and write the plan. However, these talks were historic, especially for the otherwise frozen U.S.-Iran relationship. They were not glamorous, though. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an homemade bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle in Garowe, Somalia. The blast killed six people, including four workers for UNICEF, the international children’s agency. Somalia’s President said this was an attack against the country’s future. This happened just after another attack on Sunday, where three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region. Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group, said they were responsible for Monday’s attack. The bombing happened around 8 a.m in Garowe, the capital of the Puntland region. The United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia confirmed these details.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will stay there for four weeks to work with the Australian military. Before starting his work, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of people gathered outside the memorial. Some took photos of the prince. One boy held a sign that said, "Red Heads Rule!" This was a celebration of the prince's red hair. The Australian Defence Forces said last week that Harry will work and live with members of the Australian Army. He will work with several army groups in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth.

Australia, a close ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop called the deal an "informal arrangement" and said it focuses on tracking Australians who travel to Iraq to fight for ISIS. However, one Australian lawmaker called the move "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

Initial tests on the flight data recorder, which is called the "black box," show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally used the controls to make the plane faster and going down. according to the French air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had been searching the mountainside in the French Alps for days since the Germanwings Flight 9525 crashed on March 4. The BEA said on Friday that its teams started looking at the data right away.

After a 110-day chase across the ocean, the crew of a suspected poaching ship called the *Thunder* was saved by conservationists who had been following them. The rescue happened in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of West Africa. The conservationists’ ship, the *Bob Barker*, received a distress call from the *Thunder*. This ended a long pursuit that began in the Southern Ocean. The *Thunder* is the subject of an Interpol "purple notice" for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago at 7:30 a.m. every day. Most students do the same. But Jason’s schedule is different. He is in a special program at the school. This program combines online learning with traditional classroom teaching. One-third of the 2,700 students at the school are in this program. By 2015, the school wants most students to join it. Jason is a top student. He also does many activities outside of school. He says the online work is easy to access. It helps him finish his school tasks. “I can learn by myself,” he says.

Days after a terrible attack by Al-Shabaab in Garissa, Kenya, launched airstrikes against the terrorist group in Somalia. A military source told CNN that these strikes are not revenge for last week’s massacre at Garissa University College, which killed nearly 150 people. The source said the attacks are part of ongoing military operations that began in 2111, not a response to the Garissa attack. The source spoke on Monday. It is common for Ken military sources to remain anonymous when talking to the media.

Pope Francis gave a traditional speech after Easter Mass. He reminded the world that the Vatican is its own country, and he spoke about his role as a moral leader. He was sad about the suffering caused by current wars. He called for an end to violence everywhere. He said that the fighting must to stop in Iraq and Syria. He also asked that help reach the people who need it. "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees," he said in his "urbi et orbi" address, Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

On Wednesday afternoon, Duke University students and teachers marched together, chanting, “We are not afraid. We stand together.” This happened after a rope noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. Duke officials asked anyone who knows about the noose to call campus police. The noose was found near a student center at 2 a.m. Photos of the noose were shared on social media and made many people in the community very angry. Hundreds of people gathered on the steps of Duke Chapel, which is close to where the noose was found. At a meeting there, people said, “This is not the Duke we want. This is not the Duke we are here to experience.”

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, a 29 U.S. citizen who has been accused of having connections with al Qaeda, appeared in court on Thursday. He did not enter a plea to the charges. He is accused of conspiring to provide material support to terrorists. A complaint, which was made public in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, states that he plotted to fight against American forces abroad. Al Farekh was deported from Pakistan to the United States. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd called this news something to celebrate.

The Saudi state news agency reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants in Yemen this week. This is the first known military death from Saudi Arabia’s side since it started bombing rebels in Yemen. The fight happened on Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. militants in the mountains of Yemen fired at Saudi border guards, who fired back. One guard, Cpl. Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, was killed. Ten other guards were hurt, but their injuries were not life-threatening.

I felt nervous about going to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. Because I is the only Gulf national on the CNN team, people expect me to know about camel racing, which is an old tradition in this area. I tried to wear a kandora, a traditional UAE outfit, but I feel like an outsider because my modern way of life is different from this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis, which is a meeting place. The camel owners were gathering there. The large room looked like a fancy theater. The camel owners sat on the floor eating a'aish, a traditional Arabic dish made of fish and rice. They were talking loudly and excitedly.

Havana, Cuba (CNN) – Charlie Hill sits in a dark bar on a bright sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, and he gives a nod that shows he knows you’ve been looking for him. But many people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has protected Hill from facing charges for killing a New Mexico police officer and hijating an airplane to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how, for the first time, he is thinking about leaving his safe place and going back to the United States.

On April 2, 2015, CNN Student News reported that Yemen, a Middle Eastern country with political instability, is becoming a focus of international concern. because it is a potential battleground for a proxy war. The show explained why Yemen is important to the world. They also talked about the history of April Fools' Day and how an ancient recipe might help fight a dangerous modern germ. Finally, they told the story of a woman who is helping children improve their lives. You can find the transcript of the show on this page and also request to be part of the CNN Student News Roll Call.

On April 3, 2015, CNN Student News covers international news from Switzerland, Kenya, and the Pacific Ocean. The historic drought in California is affecting residents and businesses, who are now required to reduce their water usage. The show also discusses two religious holidays being celebrated around the world this weekend, and features two stories about U.S. National Parks. All of this is included in Friday’s episode. Misao Okawa, who was recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, died at the age of 117. She passed on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to local official Tadahi Uchimura. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. She leaves behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren.

Satoshi Yoshioka, who worked at the nursing home where Okawa lived since 1997, told CNN that her family ran a kimono shop in Osaka. He described Okawa as having a gentle personality and having a big appetite. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. Yoshioka noted that she ate a lot of cake for her birthday on March 5 of

Documents obtained by CNN show that the Missouri National Guard, as they were preparing to deploy to Ferguson, Missouri, last year, used highly militarized language to describe protesters. The guard referred to them as "enemy forces" and "adversaries." The guard went to Ferguson to support law enforcement officers. Many community leaders and civil rights activists accused these officers of using excessive force and making an already tense situation worse. The protests happened sporinly from August through the end of the year.

On Tuesday, gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. This attack was two parts: a car bomb and a shooting. The attack killed at least 12 people and hurt 16 others. officials said. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. Their spokesman, Abu Musab, said Al-Shabaab was responsible. The attack started when two suicide bombers blew up a car at the entrance of the two-story building. The building houses the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Higher Education. Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said this. Then, five gunmen went into the building and shot people inside.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, fought in World War II as a 16-year-old Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army. While he was fighting the Nazis, his family fled. Margolin says he did not reveal he was Jewish, but it didn’t matter because people were being killed all around him. Now, in Ukraine, he is facing war again. Margolin was a sniper who became a commander. He still has his old uniform with medals from his military service. His granddaughter, Liora, is amazed by his war stories and how he survived.

365 days have gone by since more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken from their school in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world are responsible for allowing this to happen. We should all feel ashamed that these girls’ lives have been destroyed by violent criminals without punishment. We should also feel ashamed that people quickly stop paying attention when terrible things happen.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to stop using FM radio. In two years, the country will completely switch to digital radio. This change is happening because people are listening to digital media instead of traditional radio.

Norwegian officials say that many people in Norway, which has a population of 5 million, have already made the switch. There are only five stations available on FM radio, but there are four times as many stations on the Digital Audio Broadcasting (DAB) network. Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey stated that half of the country now listens to radio digitally.

Everyone is excited about a good comeback story, especially when it involves a dinosaur. A new study suggests that the Brontosaurus should have its own name. For over 100 years, its name was removed from science books. O.C. Marsh first gave the name "Brontosaurus" ( meaning "thunder lizard") in 1879. He did this after receiving 55 crates of bones found at Como Bluff in Wyoming. The Brontosaurus was similar to, but smaller than, the Apatosaurus, which had been discovered a few years earlier.

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 2 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for the death or capture of two prominent Shia Muslim leaders in Yemen. The group, called Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), wanted these men because they are their enemies. The reward is offered for Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. AQAP called them “the two heads of evil.” AQAP is one of many groups fighting to control Yemen.

Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old postal worker from Florida, wrote about his plans and reasons for flying a gyrocopter onto the Capitol lawn on Wednesday on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. He said his goal was to expose corruption in Washington, D.C., and to propose solutions to the problem of corruption. He wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot" that his flight was not a secret. He said he had sent an email to info@barackobama.com before taking off, hoping to convince Capitol officials that he was not a threat and that shooting him down would be more of a problem than letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The problems for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics continue. many dead fish found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. The city’s legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday to find out why the fish died. They will help with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Environment Secretariat. The investigation will look at the lagoon and other lakes and bays in the state where this has happened. The rowing and canoe competitions will take place in Rio in just over a year.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But he is just now getting used to the normal world. Small things like using a fork, going out at night, and sleeping without someone checking on him are all new experiences. Hinton spent nearly 30 years on death row in Alabama. until last week, when his murder convictions were canceled and he was released from a Birmingham jail. "I have to pinch myself to believe that I'm free," he told CNN's Brooke Baldwin on Friday. "It will take some time, but I will get used to it." Hinton had to deal with much harder things. For 30 years, he spent most of his time locked in a small 5-by-7 cell.

After the UK election debate, opinion polls showed that there was no clear winner. The seven party leaders were: David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalists). Comres, which organized the debate for ITV, found that Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first place with 21%, and Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. ICM, which worked for The Guardian, gave Miliband 25%, Cameron 24%, Farage 19%, and Sturgeon 17%.

Facebook might soon need to add a new relationship status option: "Just got served divorce papers." because a New York judge ruled that using social media to serve divorce papers is legal. Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband for several years, according to her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell. They have not been able to find Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku to give him the official papers. Court documents say Baidoo has been able to call her husband, and he has told her that he does not have a fixed address or a place of employment.

It sounds like a scene from a science fiction movie. A person gets a terrible accident, and they are in the hospital, brain dead, and on life support. The doctors ask the family to give organs to save up to eight people. But instead, the family is asked to give the whole body to save just one person. Maybe a person who is paralyzed from the neck down but has a very smart mind. This idea sounds crazy, but an Italian doctor named Sergio Canavero says we are getting close to making it happen. The project is called HEAVEN, which stands for "head anastomance venture." "anastomance" means joining two parts together with surgery.

Anthony Stokes’s story was expected to be a happy one, but it ended in tragedy on Tuesday, according to police. The teenager, who had received a heart transplant, died after his car crashed into a pole. He was on a high-speed chase with police. He had carjacked someone, broke into a home, and shot at an elderly woman.

 In 213, Stokes’s family told the media that an Atlanta hospital refused to give him a heart transplant. The hospital said in a letter that Stokes had a history of not following medical advice. Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family at that time.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had already up for early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack started.

Around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday), the attackers blew up the front gate and started shooting. They kept firing as they walked around the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a girls' dorm. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took hostages, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, was buried at New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang as a large crowd gathered to remember him. Gray died in police custody 15 days after his arrest for weapons charges. He suffered a severe spinal cord injury and died. his death caused anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray’s death is another high-profile case involving an African-American and law enforcement. People have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. Civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of others who died in police custody attended his funeral.

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I started fighting for food policy changes much later. In 2007, a young girl my wife helped was searching through trash to find food. This event made me start Food Policy Action and become involved in political issues about food, including hunger and factory farming. I have not worked alone on this. "The Meatrix," a 2003 animated video that made fun of "The Matrix" and was made by the GRACE Communications Foundation, was a major reason for change. It showed the health and environmental dangers of factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor, so he has seen many patients die in hospitals. They were often on strong pain medication and very worried. he has also watched people suffer for weeks or months while their families watched helplessly. But now, his own health is the problem. In 223, he was told he had a rare, serious type of cancer that had spread. Surge doctors removed parts of his pancreas and liver, and also took out his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows the cancer might come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and supporters of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh in Aden. The Saudi soldiers were in Aden to help organize and guide the battle, but they did not directly combat. They also helped drop weapons and communication equipment by parachute. After strong air attacks by Saudi planes, the Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important areas in the southern port city of Aden. This was a change from the previous day when the Houthi forces had taken control of the presidential palace.

A woman from Detroit, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged in court this week with murder and torture. This happened last month when police found the bodies of two of her children inside a freezer.

Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy charges that Blair killed her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, a court worker found the bodies wrapped in plastic inside the freezer on March 24. The worker was there to carry out an eviction order.

A medical examiner has determined that Stoni died from multiple blunt trauma injuries and Stephen from multiple blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the current world heavyweight boxing champion, has a big title fight coming up. However, he is mostly thinking about the ongoing struggle for democracy in his home country, Ukraine. Klitschko spoke to CNN from his training base in Miami before his match with American challenger Bryant Jennings on April 25 in New York. He said the crisis in his homeland has left him shocked and upset. "My country is unfortunately suffering in the war with Russia. It is not that Ukraine tried to give any aggression to any other nation, in this particular case Russia, unfortunately it's the other way around," Klitschko told CNN.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, making a small reference to his famous roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." This was his third time hosting the show. He joked in his opening speech that many things have changed since he first hosted the show in 182. "I had a baby—he is 31. I also have a new girlfriend—she is 28," he said.

Some fans were disappointed because they hoped to see him fully act out his most famous characters. SNL cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song asking him to play Batman and Beetlejuice with them. All he did was make a few quick jokes.

About a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell, waiting to attack. When a correctional officer came to check the cells, Taylor attacked him. Taylor beat the guard, took his uniform, and took his keys. He then walked out of the jail and got into the officer’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old was supposed to be sentenced in May. Now, no one knows where he is. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m. in some time zones).

A New York City detective has been suspended because he is accused of stealing $300 during a raid on illegal cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis made the announcement. Surveillance video from CNN affiliate News 12 Brooklyn seems to show Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes, according to News 12 Brooklyn. Ali Abdullah, the store's manager, noticed the money was missing from a box. He thought one of his employees had taken it. When he checked the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw, he told News 12 Brooklyn.

The Hatton Garden burglary, which will likely be remembered as a major crime, was a terrible experience for safe deposit box owners and a exciting scene for movie directors. Thieves broke into the vault of a well-known safe deposit company in central London over the holiday weekend. They used heavy cutting tools and climbing gear. They possibly had up to four days to search through many safe deposit boxes. They reportedly stole hundreds of thousands of pounds in gems and cash. One former police officer guessed the total value could be as much as 200 million pounds, or $300 million.

On April 27, South Africa marks the anniversary of the first elections after apartheid in 1994. This year, we are facing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are angry about this violence, and they are expressing their outrage on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica. The hashtag shows that people want to stand together against this attack. These repeated attacks on migrants and their property show that South Africa’s dream is failing. The dream was not just about having people of many different ethnic groups living together, but also about everyone, regardless of race or class, living with dignity.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, said he was “drinking poison” when he accepted a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped define his government, the Islamic Republic, which he had founded a year before Iraq’s leader, Saddam Hussein, invaded Iran. Khomeini united the country, both supporters and and opponents, to fight the enemy. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam was ready to stop fighting, and this helped make the Islamic Republic stronger. When the war ended, the economy was ruined, and his loyal volunteers were gone.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful for its own good. The global economy is growing very fast, doubling in size every generation. But this growth is a problem because Earth has limited resources. The world population adds one billion new people every 15 years. This rapid growth and capitalism are harming the natural environment and the social systems that make life good. Sustainable development offers a way to solve this growing crisis. The truth is that unchecked capitalism is driven by greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space-faring nation. U.S. access to space has provided incredible benefit to U.S. national security, defense and the economic well-being of the nation. And in order to effectively confront current and future conflicts, combat terrorism and counter the proliferating threats worldwide, our military depends on space-based capabilities, including intelligence, GPS, and communications satellites. Unfortunately, as global threats increase and the need for assured space access accelerates, the U.S. is faced with a troubling reality - we are far too reliant on Russian technology to meet our national security obligations.

On the day before the one-year anniversary of the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls in Nigeria by Boko Haram, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to the girls. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner survived an attack by the Taliban, because they wanted to stop her from blogging about the importance of girls going to school in Pakistan. She says that she was also a target of militants who did not want girls to go to school. She asks the Nigerian government and the rest of the world to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently had an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers were sent in to help the government stop deadly attacks against immigrants. Their first mission was in Jeppestown, a neighborhood in Johannesburg. where violence against immigrants started on Friday.

While soldiers were guarding the area, police searched a hostel in Jeppestown. The Defense Minister, Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula, explained that the government is sending an unknown number of soldiers to areas where the police are too busy and cannot handle the attacks on immigrants. She said that using soldiers does not mean the police are doing a bad job.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards died in fighting with militants near the Pakistan border. Iranian forces killed three of the militants in the town of Negur on Monday. The news agency IRNA reported that the militants crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials asked Pakistan to capture the surviving attackers.

Providenciales, in the Turks and Caicos, has been named the number one island in the world by TripAdvisor. It was last year's second choice. It now has the top spot, ahead of Ambergris Caye, in Belize. Ambergris Caye was the number one island for two years in a row. It has now fallen out of the top 10. Why did it drop? A TripAdvisor spokesperson, Julie Cassetina, said it is hard to say. The winners change each year based on feedback from travelers.

The "Star Wars" story continues to grow. at a fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, the plot for the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" was announced. Director Gareth Edwards showed a short preview of the film. The movie, which Disney called an "anthology" (a word they prefer instead of "spinoff"), stars Felicity Jones. The story happens between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" (the first "Star Wars" movie from 1777). A group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Jones plays a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and China—to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is a sign that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a great one indeed. Although some hard-line politicians may now try to play games and complain the preliminary agreement is not what they had hoped, for many people it shows excellent progress and that's what they want.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) – Breaking news at 11:45 p.m. ET: Two African-Americans, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This makes three of the six council members Black. (Earlier story, published at 6:52 p.m. ET): The sky looked dark and the radio warned about flash floods. It was raining, but the voting places opened at 6 a.m. for city elections. Usually, very few people come to vote. But today was different. This was the first city election since white police officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed Black teenager Michael Brown last August. Since then, this St.

On Wednesday night, one person died and another was hurt in a suspected terrorist attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. The police say a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, was taken to the hospital but he died there. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being questioned by the General Security Services.

The art collection of the late actress Lauren Bacall has been put for sale. The collection, which includes works by some of the greatest 20th-century artists, was sold in New York on March 31. It had been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before the sale. Bacall, who died in August 214 at age 99, became famous in 114 with her first movie, "To Have and Have Not." It was also during that time that she met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 215 Golden Globes, George Clooney paid tribute to the silver screen queen in his award winning speech.

People in Kiev, Ukraine, are worried about who might killing people who were close to Ukraine’s former President, Viktor Yanukovych. This fear has been around before, but it became more important this week after two famous people were shot and killed in Kiev. One was a former member of parliament who had connections to Yanukovych, and the other was a journalist who supported Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former politician, was shot and killed around 7 o'clock in the evening on Wednesday as he was entering his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday. Chile is now one of several South American countries that allows these unions. Bachelet said, "This is a concrete step in the drive to end the difference between homosexual and heterosexual couples." The new law will take effect in six months. It will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The Chilean government estimates that around 2 million people will be able to benefit from the change.

When you fly to Florida, look out the window. If you are visiting Disney World or going to Miami, sit by the window and look at the land below. It is a large swamp. This place shows how humans made mistakes and how much it cost to fix them. When you flying into Miami or Orlando, the swamp looks like a messy, empty place full of dangerous animals. There are snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One researcher once caught 365,000 mosquitoes in just one night using a single trap.

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. They came in large numbers, wearing masks, and quickly control the area. The camp had been under attack by Syrian forces for more than two years. The residents already lived in fear. Now, they faced a new, worse danger: ISIS had defeated other armed groups in the area and taken control. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS killed people in the streets. He said they caught three people and killed them in front of others. ISIS now controls almost all of the camp.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have found their "Great Firewall" isn't enough anymore. They have developed a new cyber weapon called the "Great Cannon." This tool allows them to attack servers outside of China, including ones in the United States. The study's authors say that the Great Cannon works openly and in plain sight. They believe that this obvious attack on other countries' servers will likely anger the international community, and that Beijing may have expected this reaction.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any evidence of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz committed the act. However, a spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had been suicidal before he became a pilot.

Christoph Kumpa, the spokesman, said investigators have not found any writings or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons or confessed to any plans. Medical records show that Lubitz was suicidal at one point and received psychotherapy. This was before he ever got his pilot’s license, Kumpa said.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said his group would not surrender. Abdul-Malik al-Houthi told people on television that his fighters will stay in the main cities and government buildings. He said, “Anyone who thinks we will give up is dreaming.” This statement came after more than three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. The coalition’s goal is to push back the Houthis. The Houthis took over the capital, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power. A top Saudi military official said these airstrikes have significantly weakened the Houthi group.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a large truck bomb into the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and hurt hundreds others. It is the worst act of homegrown terrorism in U.S. history. The news media covered the story heavily, talking about how America had been hurt and had lost its innocence. The bombing surprised the country. People were shocked not just by how many people died, but by the fact that an American citizen had attacked the U.S. government with such deadly force.

If you really cared about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign or join a demonstration? How long would you continue, when no one else seemed to care? A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were taken from their school by Boko Haram militants. millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people, along with celebrities and world leaders, who expressed their anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It was one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2021, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks became months, the missing girls still had not been found. the attention on the campaign faded.

Barney Frank, a retired U.S. Congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He told the full audience about his 45 years in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while holding office. He criticized politicians who hide their sexual identity and vote against gay rights. When a young man in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about it. He told the young man not to worry about crazy people.

Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on Thursday morning. during morning prayers. The attackers shot people randomly and took hostages. nearly 150 people were killed, including students, and dozens were injured. Kenyan security forces killed the attackers. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said that Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. This attack happened just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been responsible for many attacks in the region and has recruited some Americans, especially Somali-Americans from Minnesota.

A university in South Africa has removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonial leader. This happens after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town started an online campaign last month. They demanded the statue be taken down. They said Rhodes’ history is racist. Students used the hashtag #RhodesMustFall on social media. Now, the hashtag is #RhodesHasFallen. The university said on Wednesday that a heritage authority gave permission to remove the statue. The university said the statue is being moved to keep it safe while people decide what to do with it in the future.

Syria is becoming a terrible place, and the situation is getting worse. According to an opposition group, the number of people killed has doubled in just one year. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported on Thursday that 310,00 people have died since the civil war began. This number was 162,402 a year earlier, and the United Nations had estimated 70,000 deaths the year before that. The United Nations says that more than half of all Syrians are so poor that they desperately need help to survive. Food rations are being reduced because there is not enough money donated to support them.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly, looking almost shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to fight a rival. A criminal complaint says she threatened a woman on the phone this summer. She told the woman, "Leave my man alone." "Stop looking for him," she said. "I know people who can put a bomb where you live." Because of who she is, prosecutors did not think it was a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment. She denies the charge. Last December, when she left court, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A police officer in Gaza told CNN that police took a door with a drawing by British artist Banksy on Thursday. This happened after a disagreement about the sale. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, said he went to a Gaza court. He said he sold the door for only $175 U.S. dollars because he did not know it was valuable. The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the iron door. They will hold it until a court hearing date is set. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had lost everything. All he had left was a doorway and a door.

The Saudi-led coalition’s attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The coalition is gaining control, while many locals are fleeing the violence and the number of deaths is rising. Dozens of civilians have been killed. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition has destroyed Houthi air defense systems and the air forces of supporters of Yemen’s former President, Ali Abdullah Saleh. a Saudi source said that all but a few air bases and runways are no longer usable. The source also said that Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all of Yemen’s ports. the navy only allows carefully monitored non-military medical supplies to pass through its blockade.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called them a "disgrace."

Iniesta, who was a star player for Spain, started the game on the bench. He came into the match in the 76th minute. The home fans cheered and booed him.

Spain's coach, Vicente del Bosque, used a team that was not his usual choice. Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored goals in the first half. These goals helped lift the spirits of the Dutch team.

 However, Hiddink was unhappy with how Iniesta was treated. Iniesta tried to control the ball during the match

On May 21, Scotland will learn if its Euro 2016 match against Georgia in September will be played without any fans in the stadium. UEFA has started disciplinary action against the Georgian Football Federation because fans ran onto the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi. UEFA is also looking into charges that say home fans set off fireworks. It will investigate other safety problems, such as blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff not doing body searches at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan ran onto the field during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

On Wednesday, football agents were waiting to hear about new rules. starting April 1, the rules for becoming a football agent will change. Anyone can become an agent if they pay £500 for the first year. The Football Association (FA) will then charge £250 for each year they renew their license. This does not apply to agents who already have a license. The FA was supposed to put a link on their website so agents could sign up, but as of 1pm, the link was not there yet. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. These changes happened after FIFA stopped regulating agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not received his salary for three months. Since joining the club in January on an 18-month contract, he has not been paid. Uvarenko has had to ask his parents for money to pay his rent. However, he likes the club's fans, who are very passionate and unique. Uvarenko told local media that the lack of money is his biggest problem at CSKA.

David Moore, 25, was angry and lost his control on the road. He had just left his house and found himself stuck in heavy traffic face-to-face with Rafal Cegielka, 45. Rafal was driving his child to St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. A court heard that David hit Rafal in the face and then broke his car with a hockey stick. This happened in front of young children. David said he was having a bad day and got very angry.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This sad result reminds people of Spain’s terrible performance at the 2014 World Cup. Gerard Pique, a Spanish player, says that coach Vicente del Bosque should not be worried about losing three friendly matches in a row. Holland scored two early goals in Amsterdam and kept Spain from scoring, even though Spain tried hard in the second half. This game is like the 5-1 loss Spain suffered in the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, which ended Spain’s six years of being the best team in the world.

Police say a New York City mother, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany during a custody dispute. A court order forbids Berger from leaving the United States with the child. On March 22, one day after Kaia was left with her mother for a weekend visit, the pair is believed to have flown to Europe. Police are searching for them. They believe Berger and Kaia boarded a flight from New York to Germany on March 22, breaking the custody order. Police say the last time anyone saw them was at Berger’s home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21, when Kaia’s father dropped her off.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The flames and thick smoke filled the sky. The fire destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. This happened after several days of storms that knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water ran off the slope. Fire investigators said the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heath were destroyed: one was half a hectare, another was one hectare, and the largest was 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls per hour during New Year’s Eve 2012 celebrations. Paramedics were overwhelmed. In Cambridge, the Territorial Army opened a field hospital to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they handled more than 600 calls per hour at their busiest time— more than three times the usual number. In Manchester, a man collapsed on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two people walked by eating late-night takeout food. In another Manchester scene, a man stood slumped in a doorway while two women walked past celebrating the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says that his strong mind helped him get over being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers stopped playing Mignolet in December because he was having a bad season. But Mignolet came back quickly when another player, Brad Jones hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old Belgian player said he stayed positive even though he was upset about being removed from the team. Mignolet told FourFourTwo: "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, as big as plums, fell in the Southern United States. people outside to record the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, videoed the ice hitting his backyard and splashing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hail falling fast and breaking when they hit the ground. Even though it was about 80 degrees outside, the hard ice took a long time to melt. In just a few seconds, the patio was covered in white ice.

The crew of a replica pirate ship, the Liana's Ransom, was forced to leave their vessel after it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine. The ship was about 30 miles east of Portland, Canada. Coast Guard officials said that nine people were rescued by lifeboats on Tuesday. The ship had engine problems around 1:35 a.m. on Monday, and its sails got stuck around the mast.

Amazing photos show blue glowing algae along Australia's east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales. The bright neon light made one of Australia's popular beaches shine. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said the scene looks like a beautiful, magical event caused by millions of tiny plankton that produce light. A similar event happened at Manly Beach in Sydney in August 214. an ocean expert told Daily Mail Australia that people should not worry about the algae.

17 Rahul Kumar, a drunk teenager, was rescued by security guards after he jumped into a lion enclosure at a zoo in western India. The incident happened at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad. Kumar climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he would kill them. He later said he was drunk and thought he had a good chance against the animals. While sitting near the enclosure, he suddenly ran toward the lions, surprising the zoo security.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window onto a car. The incident happened last Saturday. his father believes the boy fell while he was sleepwalking. A hotel worker across the street heard a loud noise around midnight, which she thought was a car accident. The People’s Daily Online reported the story.

Drew Miller, a player for the Detroit Red Wings, said he is excited to play again. He got a cut on his face just one day ago. The cut could have made him blind. Miller said, "I feel very lucky that the skate did not hit my eye." He practiced on Wednesday. He wore a full face mask. His face had a bad wound. It needed 50 or 60 stitches to close. The stitches went through several layers of skin. The Detroit Free Press reported this. Miller has a scar across his eye. But he did not lose his eyesight. Another player cut his face with a skate.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends next year, even though Atletico Madrid might try to bring him back this summer. He joined Chelsea last July from Atletico on a three-year deal, but he has had trouble playing well as a left back at Stamford Bridge. Atletico thinks this might be an advantage in negotiations, but Luis says, “I am happy at Chelsea and I want to stay here until my contract is over.”

22-year-old Charlie Sumner, a fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from football. He was topless and doing somersaults on the field during his first game at the Madejski Stadium. Sumner, 20, jumped onto the field during the FA Cup quarter-final replay between Reading and Bradford City last month. Reading was winning 3-0 at the time. Sumner did four front flips on the field and landed on his back. before being stopped by security guards. Sumner said going to his first game was a great experience. He now faces a possible three-year ban for his stunt.

A video shows a van carrying about six men on its roof swerving and then tipping over. The accident happened on a road near Salé, Morocco. The van was likely carrying football fans. The video was recorded by a car following the van.

England’s Under-17 soccer team plays in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships. The tournament is in Bulgaria in May. They are playing against the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England’s coach is John Peacock. The team is the current champion because they beat Holland on penalties in last year’s final in Malta. To get to the quarter-finals, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has 16 teams, up from eight teams before. Danny Collinge scored England’s first goal against Norway during the qualifying matches.

An elephant was relaxing by a small pool in South Africa’s Kruger National Park with its family. A male buffalo came too close, which made the elephant angry. The elephant tried to spray the buffalo with water from its trunk to make it leave, but it missed. The baby elephant stayed close to its parent for protection while the buffalo drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, won an eight-year legal battle to overturn his conviction for showing foreign TV channels that broadcast Premier League soccer games. Thorpe, 55, was convicted in November 206 at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon, because he showed a Premier League game without an agreement with the official broadcasters. He says the long fight cost him heavily, including the loss of his pub.

The Irish Football Association (IFA) is worried about structural damage at Windsor Park, their stadium in Belfast. They hope that the problem does not prevent them from hosting a important Euro 2016 match against Romania in June. The IFA discovered cracks in the West Stand on Tuesday morning. The area is closed off while engineers check the damage. A spokesperson for the IFA said they found out about the damage that happened overnight on Monday night.

22-year-old Charlie Sumner, a football fan, is facing a three-year ban. He was topless and doing somersaults on the field during his first game at the stadium. The incident happened at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup match against Bradford City last month. Sumner, a supporter of Reading, did four front flips on the pitch while his team was leading 3-0. He landed on his back each time before being stopped by security guards.

A BMW driver was arrested today after a student was hit and killed while walking to the library. The driver had five children in the car. Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night. She was just weeks away from turning 22. Friends left flowers at the scene today. They said Miss Shamim, who was from Peterborough and went by the nickname "Hyena," was very much loved and a charming lovely girl.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested because a video of them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston was posted online. The video was recorded on Tuesday. The mother, who is not named, was angry because the student was allegedly bullying her daughter. The Channel 2 news reported this. The mother is wearing a black top on the right side of the video, and the victim is in the center wearing white.

Stoke City’s chief executive, Tony Scholes, hopes they can keep Asmir Begovic, the team’s goalkeeper. Begovic is in the final year of his contract. He has been linked with other clubs while playing at the Britannia Stadium. His current contract has just over 12 months left. Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old’s ambitions. He told The Sentinel: "Asmir is a great goalkeeper and we really want him to stay. It is natural that there will be rumors about the future of very good players."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was fired by his boss for reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver turning the pages of the newspaper while the bus was moving and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, with a complaint. The video shows the driver looking at the newspaper as the bus slows down for a traffic light. The boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s actions and called him a “complete idiot.”

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says defender Winston Reid will play on Saturday against Leicester City, because they are the last team in the league. Reid has been injured since March 4, when his hamstring hurt in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea. He has been back in full training during the break, so he is ready to play. However, Enner Valencia will not play. Valencia missed the last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of an unusual toe injury he got in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is not yet ready for a match. The picture shows Reid fighting with Tottenham’s Mousa Dembele in February. Allardyce confirmed, “We have Winston back in full training.”

Five days before his wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. Brittany died, and John was badly hurt. he survived, but his body was severely injured. doctors said he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and using a wheelchair. John was 25 and worked as an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College. Even though the situation looked very bad, John recovered. On March 24, he helped his team win a championship.

Lucas, playing on the left, was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard at the All-Star charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a midfielder for Liverpool, wants to return to his best form after recovering from an injury. The Brazilian player had a good run from late November to February, where he played 16 of 19 matches. This period also saw the team’s results improve. However, a groin injury in the Merseyside derby in February kept him out for 10 games. He did not play in the loss to Manchester United, which was the team’s first league defeat since mid-December. Lucas did play for 90 minutes in Sunday’s All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Are you tired of boring father-daughter photos? Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama has a funny way to make them more interesting. In her new photos, serious-looking teenage daughters stand still while their fathers jump in the air. The daughters look at the camera and smile, while their fathers make dramatic jumping poses. These pictures are from Aoyama’s latest book, which is called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man, who is between 50 and 60 years old, for robbing a bank. He took £3,000 in cash and ran away. The robbery happened at 12:30 pm at a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater, Cardiff. The police showed pictures from security cameras of the man. He is between 5 feet 9 inches and 6 feet tall. He was wearing black clothes. The man is white, has black hair with some grey, and wore glasses. No one was hurt during the robbery. The police are sure that people will recognize him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ended Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations. The ban was originally imposed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Morocco was kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and was fined $1 million. CAF also asked for an extra $9 million in compensation because Morocco withdrew as host due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. The 2017 tournament was won by Ivory Coast, which was held in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco can now take part in the next two African Cup of Nations.

Tom Boyd thinks that Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he is now ready to compete for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would be bad news for Celtic manager Ronny Deila, who wanted to keep the young Belgian player for another year. Boyd sees a positive side, though: he believes Denayer’s success will encourage other young players to choose Celtic for their next career step. 19-year-old defender Jason Denayer has done well during his loan season at Celtic. He recently earned his first cap for the Belgian national team in a Euro 22 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a amazing goal for England in Italy, and he said that critics like Paul Merson were exactly the motivation he needed. This has been a difficult season for the 23-year-old, who hasn’t been playing as well as he did when he first became an international player. England manager Roy Hodgson still believed in him, and Townsend proved that belief was right by scoring a great goal at Juventus Stadium. England tied Italy 1-1 in a friendly match in Turin on Tuesday. Townsend celebrated his goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish football team Atletico Madrid. This was confirmed at a special meeting on Tuesday. Wanda’s legal team signed the deal for 726,707 shares costing €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to approve it. Wang Jianlin, chairman of Wanda Group, wants to make Atletico Madrid more popular in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, spoke to the press.

Antonio Conte said that his return to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 draw against England was a happy memory. despite reports that he received death threats in the days before the friendly. Conte became Italy’s manager in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli. after Italy’s failure to advance out of the group stage at last summer’s World Cup. His first seven months as national team coach have been very difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to tie Bulgaria 2-2 last Saturday. Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after midfielder Claudio Marchisio injured his knee the day before the Euro 216 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that the final month of the Scottish Championship season could be easier for Hibernian (Hibs) than for Rangers. His team, Dumbarton, has already played both of his former clubs this season and will face them again in the coming weeks.

Although Rangers are currently winning games and have momentum, Murray does not believe they can keep up their fast pace until the end of the season. He expects the advantage to shift back to Hibernian soon.

Simon Mignolet, the goalkeeper for Liverpool, posted photos of himself sitting in an airplane cockpit with pilots on his Facebook page. He was returning to England after playing for the Belgian national team in Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Although Mignolet was named in the team for both games, he did not play. Belgium’s manager, Marc Wilmots, chose Chelsea’s goalkeeper, Thibaut Courtois, instead. Mignolet has played 14 times for Belgium so far.

Chyknell Hall Estate, a large country property near Bridgnorth in Shropshire, is for sale. The price is £6 million. The estate covers 200 acres. It includes a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms. It was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice since it was built. The estate also has a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and a cricket pitch. The large, private grounds offer complete privacy, which could attract famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas are on administrative leave after a video showed them harassing four students and arresting one. The video shows the officers hitting the student before arresting him. The incident happened at El Centro College in downtown Dallas. It was recorded by student Charles Adams. Adams was standing outside the campus, smoking a cigarette, when he saw what happened. The officers approached the students while they were waiting for a bus. The event took place last Wednesday.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke the permanent manager. He signed a three-year contract. Locke, 39, was the assistant manager at the club last summer. He worked under Allan Johnston. Locke became the head coach in early February when Johnston left. Locke was Johnston’s former teammate at Hearts. Locke was also the manager of Hearts before that. Since Locke took charge, Kilmarnock has played seven games and lost only once. Locke will speak to reporters at a press conference on Friday morning.

This weekend, one of the biggest events in German football happens. The usual excitement for this match, recently called "Der Klassiker," has been lessened. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five Bundesliga titles. Bayern Munich is expected to continue its success in Germany this season. However, these two teams are now far apart in the standings. There is a 31 point difference and nine places between them. Even though they are far apart, the importance of this game remains high, as it always is when these two clubs play each other. Jurgen Klopp, the manager of Borussia Dortmund, is shown celebrating with his players after they beat Hannover.

14-year schoolgirl Deva Joseph was stuck at London Stansted airport when easyJet refused to let her on her flight to Spain. Because she had two carry-on bags, the airline said she couldn't board. Deva offered to pay extra to check the second bag, but was told they only accept credit cards. She doesn't have a credit card because she is too young.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head. The hit was so hard that people heard a "cracking" sound. Robson was drunk after attending his grandfather’s funeral. He attacked Potts outside a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November last year. Potts had stepped in to stop a fight. Robson has a history of violent crimes. He was sentenced to three and and half years in jail.

Scoring a goal against your old team and taking a perfect free kick are two of the best feelings in football. Notts County player Ellen White had both happen at once on Thursday night. She played against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County won a free kick near the penalty area. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood seemed to confuse each other, almost running into one another. Ellen White took the free kick and scored into the corner. This was especially satisfying because Arsenal was her former team.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. 68 girls, aged 16 to 18, from Huizhou Integrated High School’s 27th March campus are taking part in the training. They are taught by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The girls are doing eight high-intensity movements, shouting ““kill, stab, slash, and jab”” as they move. The People’s Daily Online reported the story. School official Huang Anruo said the knives are fake, not real ones, to keep everyone safe.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. Most people don’t think about what their mind and body needs during this rest time to feel refreshed each day. The Sleep Health Foundation has released a study that shows 30 percent of Australians say they get not enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman, who is the chair of the foundation, says that if we miss out on sleep, we have to make up for it later to stay functional throughout the week. Another study confirms that 30 percent of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep each day. The average adult needs about eight hours of sleep each night, with a healthy range between seven and nine hours.

A video shows a fight between neighbors in Perth, Australia. It ends with someone getting hurt by a crowbar. The video was posted on Facebook today. It shows an angry woman yelling at a group of men who appear to be African. She is standing behind her fence. She uses racist words. Then, she goes into her neighbor’s front yard. She holds a metal crowbar. She yells at the men and swings the crowbar at them. The men pick up their own weapons. A fight starts. The woman yells, ““I don’t deal with monkeys. Go away, you f*****g monkeys.”

Valencia’s 19-year-old left back, Jose Luis Gaya, is attracting interest from Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea. These English clubs want to sign him before Real Madrid can. Sportsmail’s Pete Jenson explains why English teams are interested. Gaya’s release clause is £13.5 million. This is a good deal, especially since Luke Shaw, who is about the same age and has similar potential, cost £27 million. However, some people worry that Gaya might not be ready for the Premier League. The picture shows Gaya playing for Valencia against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to find a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. The incident happened in Salem. a 59 man named Edward West allegedly pulled a gun on the teens and told them, "get ready to die." A stranger on a green motorcycle rode up and hit the gun out of West's hands with his helmet. This allowed the teens to run away. The police are looking for the motorcyclist to thank him and identify him.

Tim Sherwood, the manager of Aston Villa, wants his team captain, Ron Vlaar, to show he can play well again. Vlaar is returning to the team after recovering from an injury. Sherwood hopes that Vlaar will help the team, which is having a difficult season, to avoid being relegated from the league. Sherwood also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten how well he played for the Netherlands in the World Cup last year. Even though he missed a penalty during a shootout against Argentina, he was still a key player in the Netherlands' journey to the semi-finals. This performance led to rumors that Manchester United might sign him. Now, the club captain is back and ready to help Aston Villa in their upcoming match against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about the club being sold this summer. He wants to build a team his way next season, if the team stays in the league. Randy Lerner, the current owner, is talking with someone who might buy the club. Some people think Sherwood might lose his job if a new owner takes over. But Sherwood is focused on keeping the team in the league. After that, he wants to make long-term plans during the summer break.

Celtic wants to loan Jason Denayer from Manchester City again next season. But, it might not happen. Manchester City’s manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said that his young players are not ready to play in the first team. So, players like Denayer might come back from loans to help the team.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting to know exactly when Fraser Forster will return from his knee injury before deciding if the club needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had surgery after twisting his knee during a 2-0 win against Burnley two weeks ago. doctors think he could be back in anywhere from four to 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a specific date for Forster’s return. He believes Kelvin Davis can do a good job as the backup keeper, but he admits he might have to find another goalkeeper if Forster takes longer to recover.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was angry on the sidelines because his team, which is in danger of being relegated, lost a close game against Birmingham City in the Sky Bet Championship. The home team, Birmingham, took the lead with first-half goals by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored a goal for Rotherham, who are currently in fourth place. However, the game was controversial. around the 55 minute mark, Birmingham player Rob Kiernan handled the ball with his hand while trying to stop Derbyshire. Derbyshire fell down in the penalty area, but the referee, Dean Whitestone, did not award a penalty kick. Evans was very upset by this decision. Birmingham held on to win the game. Robert Tesche was shown celebrating

Virgil van Dijk, a defender for Celtic, is worried about his chances of playing for the Netherlands national team. The Dutch team has already allowed more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they lost in all of their qualifying matches for the last World Cup. However, national team manager Guus Hiddink has not contacted him. Van Dijk was selected for two national team squads last year, but he was not chosen again. While the Dutch team was playing a 1-1 tie against Turkey, Van Dijk was on vacation in the Arabian Gulf with his teammates from his club. Even though he has been playing very well for Celtic, he did not receive a call-up to the national team.

Celtic has complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness at Hampden later this month. The SFA has already been criticized by Inverness fans for scheduling the match for 12:15 pm on Sunday, April 18, before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. Now, Celtic has made its feelings known. The ticket prices are £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults and £5 for concessions in the East Stand.

Paul Murray, the interim chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday that the previous management team is completely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The team will be forced to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because they cannot find a new advisor to meet the rules. Murray said that the new board’s future plans and planned investments will still happen as expected.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how the team started their match in Italy on Tuesday night.
